labels.label: theo:geroch_sing
labels.notes: Covers only the « Moreover » (ETT.tex:1778, proof l.1787-1795), status partial, unmarked: correct. LEAN >= PAPER on what it covers. Paper: M a singular flat spacetime (connected, Hausdorff, second countable l.254-255, strongly causal by DEC-18), Sigma a Cauchy surface, conclusion M homeomorphic to Sigma x R. Lean (SingularRowsSplitting.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow, :102): SingularGXStructure + T2 + second countable + C absolutely minimal with IsoChartsCoverDEC25 (the DEC-25/OQ-18 reading inherited from SingularRowsCauchy), C causal (weaker than strongly causal), connectedness dropped, S an IsCauchySurface (DEC-14, the ruled form: the printed 'every causal curve' form admits none), and one ADDED named hypothesis, a causal flow phi. Conclusion: a mathlib Homeomorph S x R ≃ₜ M (subspace topology on S, product topology), with psi(x,t) = phi t x and IsCauchySplitting; Nonempty (S x R ≃ₜ M) is the printed form (nonempty_homeomorph_of_isCausalFlow). The added flow is the content of lem:vecteur (not formalized), disclosed in the REPORT (hypothesis row 'strengthened'), in both SCOPEs, and is why the row is partial: acceptable under kb/0012 and kb/0022. Q1, IsCausalFlow AGAINST lem:vecteur's flow (l.1751-1758, 1788-1793): IsCausalFlow (Causal/Splitting.lean:129) asks a Flow R M (a continuous complete R-action), every orbit t -> phi t x an inextensible (DEC-11) causal curve over univ, and no fixed point. The paper's Phi satisfies each: complete by l.1788-1789, inextensible causal orbits by l.1793 (asserted for x in Sigma, but X is causal everywhere, so for every x), and no fixed point because X is non-singular (l.1754). So IsCausalFlow is implied by every reading of the paper's flow: it is a weaker hypothesis, which gives a stronger theorem. C1 and parallelism at sing(M) are not used. IsCausalFlow.of_causalCurveIn shows that on a T2 space inextensibility even follows from the causal orbits and the absence of fixed points. The question is MOOT as a reading (no OQ row): what remains is an unproved lemma (lem:vecteur), not an ambiguity. CONVERSE (a): IsCausalFlow.toVecteurFlow (SingularSplitting.lean:260) takes the causal flow, SingularFlatAxioms and C causal. Its fields: flow x t := phi t x; continuity; flow_zero; flow_add; inextensible from hphi; injective from IsCausalFlow.injective under the supplied causality; isOpenMap for every Cauchy S from isOpenMap_of_isCausalFlow. Correctly stated. nonempty_vecteurFlow_iff (:278) is the equivalence at a causal SFA spacetime, every theorem's setting. VecteurFlow.isCausalFlow (:126) uses causality only for « no fixed point », as its SCOPE says. The 'any psi' reading (Q3) is moot: see lem:Sigma_separe. WITNESSES (kb/0011): tauFlow is a genuine causal flow. isCausalFlow_tauFlow proves its orbits are CausalCurveIn over univ via E0.le_iff_closed at equal radius and angle, and non-stationarity from x.1 + 1 ≠ x.1. Its null orbits (not_lt_tauFlow: ClosedLt asks rad x < rad x) and not_isChronalFlow_tauFlow are real. Every E0 instance derives from the M-level theorems: tauFlow_split and nonvacuous_e0 go through exists_sigma_separe_of_isCausalFlow at M; nonvacuous_e0_natural through rows_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25, so through K_ordre_Sigma_of_isCausalFlow and nonempty_vecteurFlow_iff at M; e0_not_hasChronalCausalFlow through the M-level not_hasChronalCausalFlow. nonvacuous_e0 exhibits a Cauchy surface with a BTZ point p in J+(S)\S, I-(p) = ∅, so the BTZ branch is exercised. vecteurFlow_e0 inhabits VecteurFlow, and the strict SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing_split is instantiated with it. Q2 (X_0 read as d/dtau): MOOT for every Lean statement, since the witness is proved a causal flow directly, whatever X_0 is. It is load-bearing only for the first sentence of REPORT finding 3, and there it is OQ-34's reading, not a new one (see findings).

labels.label: lem:Sigma_separe
labels.notes: Covers the equalities J^±(Sigma) = psi(Sigma x R_±) (ETT.tex:2066). It also restates the « In particular » (l.2067-2068) from T-ett-sigma-separe. Status partial, unmarked: correct. LEAN >= PAPER: sigma_separe_of_isCausalFlow (SingularSplitting.lean:288; at M, SingularRowsSplitting.lean:144) weakens globally hyperbolic to causal and keeps Sigma Cauchy (DEC-14). It quantifies over every causal flow phi and every homeomorphism psi : S x R ≃ₜ M with psi(x,t) = phi t x, and concludes both equalities plus the « In particular ». The model-free IsCausalFlow.Jplus_eq_image / Jminus_eq_image (:154, :174) give the equalities as sets for any causal flow, causal C and acausal Cauchy S, with no homeomorphism and no closedness. Acausality is an extra hypothesis only in that model-free form: under SFA it is derived (IsCauchySurface.isAcausal_of_t1_secondCountable), as the REPORT says. Q3, « the homeomorphism of Theorem theo:geroch_sing » (l.2064): MOOT, no OQ row. Every choice of X in lem:vecteur gives a psi of the quantified form, by the argument under theo:geroch_sing. Independently, the strict IsCauchySplitting.Jplus_eq (Causal/CauchyDiamond.lean) already covers any psi with psi(x,0) = x and monotone lines. The REPORT finding (l.2063-2066) is true and kernel-checked: neither GH nor psi being a homeomorphism is needed for the set equalities. It honestly notes that for singular flat spacetimes the gain is in the route, since GH follows from (iii)=>(i) in the paper (OQ-32).

imports_comment: Dispatch item 7. Causal.Splitting is the only home of IsCausalFlow and IsCausalFlow.exists_isCauchySplitting, and the dispatch listed it among the consumed modules. Re-deriving IsCausalFlow would duplicate a structure the strict splitting theorem consumes, and hoisting it needs an edit to Causal/Splitting.lean, which the dispatch forbids. So the import is the right call. Measured over the in-repo import graph: relative to Causal.SingularCauchy, Causal.Splitting adds exactly Causal.Chains, Causal.Flat.Form, Causal.Flat.IsomCausal, Causal.GXStructure, Causal.Minkowski, Causal.Splitting and Causal.Static (plus mathlib's manifold and ODE modules). That is exactly the list in the SCOPE 'Imports' bullet (SingularSplitting.lean:84-90). SingularRowsSplitting adds nothing, since Causal.Remarks.SingularRowsCauchy's closure already contains Causal.Splitting. The SCOPE bullet is honest. Two sentences are not: the header sentence at l.10 and the closing claim of the same bullet (finding 1).

findings.what: Two claims overstate the model-freeness. (i) The header says « This module imports no model. » without 'directly'. Through Causal.Splitting the module transitively imports Causal.Minkowski, Causal.Static and Causal.Flat.*, which the SCOPE bullet at l.84-88 correctly says. (ii) The SCOPE (l.89-90) and kb_proposal 5 claim « The closure becomes model-free once IsCausalFlow and the hitting-time splitting are hoisted out of Causal.Splitting ». Hoisting would not achieve that. tools/ladder.py:668 (MODEL_LAYER) counts Causal.SingularFlat as model layer, and this module reaches it independently of Causal.Splitting, through Causal.SingularCauchy -> Causal.SingularGeroch -> Causal.SingularFlat. The docstring convention of Causal.SingularCauchy (« imports no model », with SingularFlatAxioms read as abstract under kb/0012) differs from the gate's definition, and the SCOPE should not assert the gate-level property.
findings.fix: At graduation: l.10 -> « This module imports no model directly (SCOPE, Imports). » In l.89-90 and the kb proposal, say that hoisting would remove Minkowski, Static, Flat and GXStructure from the closure, while Causal.SingularFlat (MODEL_LAYER in tools/ladder.py) stays, through Causal.SingularCauchy.

findings.what: The finding's first sentence, « The flow of the vertical field X_0, read as the τ-translation of Causal.E0, is null at every point of E₀ », holds in OQ-34's reading of E₀ (metric −2dτdr + dr² + r²dθ², Causal.Port.E0Model). Under the metric the paper prints, −dτ² + dr² + r²dθ² (ETT.tex:1329-1330), ∂_τ is timelike everywhere. The finding names only 'Causal.E0'; OQ-34 appears only in question 2, yet findings go to the author as facts. The rest of the finding does not depend on the reading and is true: no chronal flow exists once a BTZ point has I⁻ = ∅, which the paper prints at l.1347 (IsChronalFlow.Iminus_nonempty, SingularFlatAxioms.not_isChronalFlow), so the classical timelike-flow closure of J^±(Σ) is unavailable.
findings.fix: Write « in OQ-34's reading of E₀ (metric −2dτdr + dr² + r²dθ²) » into the finding's first sentence. File no new OQ: Q2 is subsumed by OQ-34.

findings.what: « Strictly weaker than the former named hypothesis VecteurFlow » contradicts the module's own nonempty_vecteurFlow_iff: at a causal SingularFlatAxioms spacetime, the setting of every theorem here, the two are equivalent. Outside that setting neither implies the other: VecteurFlow -> IsCausalFlow needs causality, and IsCausalFlow -> VecteurFlow needs SFA for the openness. The docstrings say 'weaker' (SingularRowsSplitting.lean:59) or 'weakened against VecteurFlow: no openness, no injectivity field' (SingularSplitting.lean:65), which is accurate as a statement about fields.
findings.fix: Write « weaker as an assumption (no openness or injectivity field); equivalent to VecteurFlow at a causal SFA spacetime (nonempty_vecteurFlow_iff) ».

findings.what: The docstring « E₀ has no chronal flow at all » and the SCOPE's « no flow of E₀ is » describe e0_not_hasChronalCausalFlow, whose statement is ¬ HasChronalCausalFlow, i.e. no flow that is both causal and chronal. The stronger ∀ φ, ¬ IsChronalFlow φ is true, by SingularFlatAxioms.not_isChronalFlow at E₀'s SFA instance, but it is not what this declaration states.
findings.fix: Either state ∀ φ : Flow ℝ E0, ¬ E0.causality.IsChronalFlow φ (one line from SingularFlatAxioms.not_isChronalFlow and SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms), or reword to « no chronal causal flow ».

report_findings_checked: theo:geroch_sing finding 1 (l.1792) is TRUE as a finding about the proof. « ψ is a local diffeomorphism » needs Σ to be a differentiable submanifold transverse to X, and a DEC-14 Cauchy surface is only a set. The topological replacement, J^±(Σ) closed ⟺ the flow splitting exists, is kernel-checked (IsCausalFlow.isClosed_iff_exists_isCauchySplitting). The paper derives the closedness only afterwards, from ψ (l.2067, l.2079). Finding 2 (order of results) is a suggestion and is accurate. Finding 3 is true, with the OQ-34 caveat above. The lem:Sigma_separe finding (l.2063-2066) is TRUE and kernel-checked, and correctly hedged.
